summary.headline: Modis Navnirman Q2 FY27 revenue rose to INR69.38 crore (QoQ up ~19%) with PAT of INR10.54 crore; H1 revenue up 53% YoY to INR127.64 crore.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 revenue from operations was INR69.38 crore versus INR58.26 crore in Q1, with EBITDA up 25% QoQ to INR14.5 crore and PAT of INR10.54 crore. H1 FY27 revenue grew 53% YoY to INR127.64 crore, EBITDA 63% to INR26.19 crore and PAT to INR19.08 crore. Management cited H1 sales of about 78,560 sq ft worth INR202 crore at an average realisation of INR25,724 per sq ft. Management said H1 operating cash flow was negative (about INR16.51 crore, per an analyst's figure), which it attributed to inventory build-up and project costs, with cash-flow positivity expected around FY28.

segments.name: Residential-cum-commercial redevelopment (Mumbai and adjoining regions)
segments.commentary: Portfolio of 25 projects covering about 29.83 lakh sq ft: 14 completed (7.22 lakh sq ft), 6 ongoing (12.11 lakh sq ft) and 5 upcoming (about 10.5 lakh sq ft). All five upcoming projects are residential-cum-commercial.

segments.name: Ongoing projects construction progress (as of Sep 2026)
segments.commentary: Rashmi Square 80% complete, Rashmi Signature 61%, Rashmi Delight 55%, Rashmi Manorath 51%. Rashmi Icon and Rashmi Avenue started in H1, at about 7.5% to 9% complete.

guidance_outlook: Management expects Q3 FY27 to be better than FY26, citing festive demand pick-up after Navratri.
Targeted completion of about INR200 crore of revenue from projects by 31 March 2027, mainly Rashmi Signature, Rashmi Manorath and Rashmi Delight.
EBITDA margin expected to stay around 19-20% on average, with management saying margins will improve from here; EBITDA targeted above the FY26 level of about INR26 crore.
Expected to be cash-flow positive around FY28 (initially said FY27, then corrected to FY28).
Target to procure more than INR500 crore of GDV per year; five upcoming projects with GDV of about INR1,000 crore to be self-funded with no debt planned.
Rashmi Paradise launch targeted for 30 October 2026 at INR27,000-30,000 per sq ft; Rashmi Square OC application planned for December 2026.
capex_capacity: Sales book of about INR202 crore on ongoing projects as of 30 Sep 2026: INR156 crore of revenue yet to be recognised from committed sales plus about INR505 crore of potential value from unsold units, totalling about INR661 crore of visibility (not a timing guarantee).
Rashmi Icon and Rashmi Avenue (started in H1) carry about INR300 crore of unsold inventory; Rashmi Icon GDV about INR180 crore with 25-30% booked.
Rashmi Paradise agreement signed; the other three upcoming projects' development agreements expected to be signed after Diwali.
Upcoming projects: Rashmi Paradise (Malad), Rashmi Sheetal (Borivali), Rashmi Royale (Kandivali), Rashmi Aurca (Khar), and Govind Dalvi Nagar.
Major cost components are government statutory approvals and construction cost; projects are self-funded from sales collections.
demand_pricing: H1 FY27 sales of about 78,560 sq ft and INR202 crore; average realisation of INR25,724 per sq ft, said to be improving.
Rashmi Paradise expected price band of INR27,000-30,000 per sq ft, which management said would lift average realisations.
H1 sales split: about 40% from newly launched Rashmi Icon and Rashmi Avenue, about 60% from ongoing projects (per management, approximate).
Rashmi Signature H1 sales about 18,500 sq ft, Rashmi Icon about 22,000 sq ft, Rashmi Square about 13,500 sq ft.

Competition: large developers target South Mumbai and larger western-suburb parcels (above 5,000 sq m); small and regional developers target smaller parcels. Management said it is selective on location, yield and margin.
Commercial components are said to speed realisation (6-12 months vs 2-2.5 years for residential).

qa_highlights.question: How is festive demand trending versus H1, and can the three near-complete projects be funded from collections?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said festive demand picked up after Navratri and Q3 should beat FY26. Rashmi Square is nearly done; Rashmi Signature is targeted for completion by March 2027 with collections mainly in Q4; Manorath and Delight will be funded from sales, so no external funding is needed.

qa_highlights.question: Which projects drove the 273% sales-value growth in H1 and what is the outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Rashmi Signature was a major driver, along with Rashmi Icon and Rashmi Avenue, which were launched this year; pre-launch bookings were recorded at launch. Rashmi Icon is about 25-30% booked and the balance of both projects is left for later quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Is the company debt-free and how far can it scale?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the five upcoming projects (GDV about INR1,000 crore) will be self-funded with no debt. Debt would only be considered for a large land parcel purchase. Procurement target is more than INR500 crore GDV a year.

qa_highlights.question: Will margins improve and what is the Paradise launch pricing?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects margins to improve as projects near completion and sale per sq ft rises. Rashmi Paradise launch is planned for 30 October 2026 at about INR27,000-30,000 per sq ft, which would lift average realisations.

qa_highlights.question: Why is operating cash flow negative in H1 despite strong profits?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to inventory and project cost build-up. Rashmi Icon and Rashmi Avenue hold major unsold inventory (about INR300 crore). Cash-flow positivity is expected in FY28, though management first said FY27 before correcting itself.

qa_highlights.question: How do competitors and project economics differ?
qa_highlights.answer: Large developers focus on South Mumbai and big parcels; the company competes on western-suburb parcels above 5,000 sq m (about 1 acre). Margins differ by location, realisation, government benefits and ready reckoner rate; blended EBITDA margin is about 19-20%.

qa_highlights.question: Expected H2 completion revenue and execution risks?
qa_highlights.answer: Management put H2 completion revenue at about INR200 crore, targeted by 31 March 2027. It said no delays or cost overruns were seen and it sees no major execution hurdles.

risks_watch: Negative H1 operating cash flow (about INR16.51 crore per an analyst's figure), driven by inventory build-up; the expected turn to positive cash flow has shifted from FY27 to FY28.
Concentration of H2 revenue (about INR200 crore) in a few near-complete projects; completion by 31 March 2027 is a key test.
Revenue visibility of INR661 crore includes INR505 crore of unsold units; management calls it visibility, not timing certainty.
Development agreements for three of five upcoming projects are still pending (expected after Diwali); Rashmi Paradise launch on 30 October 2026 needs to hold at INR27,000-30,000 per sq ft.
Competition from large and regional developers for bigger western-suburb parcels; Mumbai supply pipeline and absorption rate.
Rashmi Square OC application expected December 2026.
summary.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on growth, margins, pricing and no-debt funding, with a few answers that were loose or self-corrected (cash-flow timing shifted from FY27 to FY28). Management was more cautious on revenue timing, calling the INR661 crore a visibility measure rather than a guarantee.
key_quotes: We don't build walls, we build homes.
So, overall, if you will see, the total revenue from the current projects, which is unsold and the revenue recognition from the committed sales, which we have already done.
We view this as a measure of revenue visibility rather than a guarantee of timing.
We are not seeking growth simply for the sake of scale.

adds.what: Upcoming residential-cum-commercial redevelopment projects (about 10.5 lakh sq ft across 5 projects, incl. Rashmi Paradise agreement signed); not physical plant

growth.why: Management guides ~INR200 crore revenue from projects completing by 31 Mar 2027 (Rashmi Signature, Manorath, Delight), a Q3 FY27 result better than FY26, and EBITDA above FY26's ~INR26 crore, backed by a INR156 crore committed sales book plus ~INR505 crore unsold potential, though no physical capacity is being added and the sales-value figures are analyst-cited.
